summary: The reported symptom (payment failures with a green error-rate dashboard) is caused by an expired mTLS client certificate on payment-service. The client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z (predicted by a cert-watcher WARN at 11:50:26Z). From 12:15:27Z payment-service logs mTLS handshake rejections and 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45)', bank_api_error_rate rises to 100%, and payment_success_rate collapses from ~99% to ~2.5%. The HTTP error-rate panel stayed flat (~0.2%) because failed payments are accepted and marked PENDING_RETRY rather than returning 5xx. Alternatives (partner-side outage, the cfg-2502 timeout change at 11:20, resource/capacity saturation, the settlement-service deploy) do not fit the timing or the error messages.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Expired payment-service mTLS client certificate to bank-partner-api
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The payment-service client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z. Once expired, mTLS handshakes to the bank-partner-api are rejected (TLS alert 45), so nearly all fund transfers fail; payments are accepted and marked PENDING_RETRY, so the HTTP 5xx error-rate panel stayed flat while ~97.5% of payments fail.

causal_chain.claim: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected with 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'
Failed payments marked PENDING_RETRY instead of returning 5xx, so error_rate stays green

assumptions: cert-watcher notAfter value is authoritative for the cert actually presented in the TLS handshake
bank-partner-api rejects (rather than silently accepts) an expired client cert

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bank-partner-api side outage / partner dependency failure
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external bank-partner-api began returning errors/failing, causing payment failures on the partner side.
assumptions: Partner outage coinciding with our cert expiry
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Logs name OUR expired certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) as the cause, not partner-side errors; onset matches cert expiry to the minute. Partner has no telemetry and there is no partner-side 5xx evidence.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config change cfg-2502 (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000) caused payment failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Raising the bank API timeout at 11:20 caused payments to fail.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Failure onset (12:15) is 55 min after cfg-2502 and coincides exactly with the cert notAfter time; a longer timeout cannot cause TLS 'expired certificate' rejections, and latency actually fell rather than rose.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource exhaustion / capacity saturation in payment-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: CPU, memory, DB pool or traffic overload caused the failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: CPU ~30%, memory ~55%, db_pool ~8 conns, restarts 0 and request_rate flat; no resource pressure at all.

facts.statement: payment-service HTTP error_rate stayed flat ~0.22% (max 0.32%) the whole window, so the panel is green.
A cert-watcher warned at 11:50:26Z that CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expires at notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z.
mTLS handshake rejections to bank-partner-api began at 12:15:27Z (140 occurrences of 'marked PENDING_RETRY').
171 log lines report 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z'.
payment_success_rate fell from ~99% to 2.47% by the 12:24 bucket and stayed ~2.5%.
bank_api_error_rate rose to 100% from the 12:24 bucket onward.
request_rate stayed flat ~100 req/s; CPU/memory/db_pool/restarts all healthy.
The only config change was cfg-2502 raising bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 11:20; latency fell, not rose.
The only deployment was settlement-service dep-5510 (v1.9.0, CSV exporter) at 10:30, unrelated to the payment path.
api-gateway error_rate stayed flat ~0.21%, showing no client-facing 5xx spike.
bank-partner-api is external with no telemetry.
Past incident HIST-106 was a settlement-service client certificate expiry with no renewal automation.

assumptions: cert-watcher's notAfter value reflects the certificate actually presented in the TLS handshake.
bank-partner-api rejects (does not silently accept) an expired client certificate.
PENDING_RETRY payments are not counted as HTTP 5xx by the dashboard, explaining the green panel.

timeline.event: cert-watcher warns client cert expires in 25 minutes
First mTLS handshake rejection to bank-partner-api; payments marked PENDING_RETRY
Latest data; success rate still ~2.5%, cert not yet rotated

recommended_actions.action: Renew/rotate the payment-service client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) and reload it immediately to restore mTLS to bank-partner-api.
recommended_actions.rationale: The cert expired at 12:15:00Z and is the direct cause of 100% bank API error rate.

recommended_actions.action: Replay the payments currently queued as PENDING_RETRY once mTLS is restored, and reconcile ledger state.
recommended_actions.rationale: Failed transfers are held as PENDING_RETRY and must be retried/reconciled for customers.

recommended_actions.action: Add a payment-success-rate / bank_api_error_rate alert and fix the error-rate panel to count PENDING_RETRY business failures, not just HTTP 5xx.
recommended_actions.rationale: The HTTP 5xx panel stayed green while 97.5% of payments failed; the monitoring gap delayed detection.

recommended_actions.action: Automate certificate expiry monitoring with paging alerts well before notAfter and implement automated cert renewal (e.g., cert-manager).
recommended_actions.rationale: cert-watcher only emitted a WARN 25 min before expiry and HIST-106 was the identical cert-expiry pattern.

data_gaps: No direct telemetry from bank-partner-api (has_telemetry=false), so partner-side acceptance of retried payments is unverified.
The PENDING_RETRY queue depth / Kafka produce metrics were not inspected, so the size of the backlog awaiting replay is unknown.
Exact error-code mapping of PENDING_RETRY to customer-visible failure is inferred from success-rate and logs, not from an explicit API response sample.
The payment-service logs were truncated (316 matched, 40 returned); the full set was not exhaustively reviewed, though the dominant patterns are consistent.

A cert-watcher WARN at 11:50:26Z reported the payment-service client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expires at notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, 25 minutes later.

findings.statement: From 12:15:27Z payment-service logged mTLS handshake rejections with bank-partner-api, e.g. 'payment 45f233b6 marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected'; the pattern repeats 140 times.

findings.statement: payment-service logs report the remote error explicitly: 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z', 171 occurrences.

refs.quote: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z

findings.statement: payment-success-rate collapsed from ~99% (12:00 bucket) to 26.82% at 12:12 and ~2.5% from the 12:24 bucket onward, staying at ~2.5% through 13:48.
bank_api_error_rate for payment-service jumped from ~0.2% to 75.05% at the 12:12 bucket and 100% from 12:24 onward.
request_rate for payment-service stayed flat at ~100 req/s across the window, so there was no traffic surge triggering the failure.
payment-service CPU (~30%), memory (~55%), db_pool_in_use (~8 conns) and restarts (0) were all flat and healthy throughout - no resource exhaustion or restart.

A config change cfg-2502 on payment-service raised bank.api.timeout_ms from 3000 to 5000 at 11:20:00Z; latency_p99_ms actually DECREASED from ~325ms to ~140ms after 12:12, so the timeout change does not explain the failure.

The only code deployment in the window was dep-5510 on settlement-service (v1.9.0, 'new CSV exporter', at 10:30:00Z), not payment-service; settlement-service logs show only benign GC pauses and an NTP resync.
api-gateway error_rate stayed flat at ~0.21% and it logged only one benign retry WARN, so the client-facing edge shows no 5xx spike either.
bank-partner-api is an external dependency with has_telemetry=false, so the fault is on the payment-service side using an expired client credential, not telemetry from the partner.
Prior incident HIST-106 (2025-06-30, settlement-service) had the same pattern: 'Client certificate expired; no renewal automation', category credential_expiry.

refs.quote: Client certificate expired; no renewal automation

findings.statement: Only ~2.5% of payments complete successfully, consistent with customer reports of ~40 failed fund transfers; failures occur while HTTP 5xx stays low because requests are accepted then marked PENDING_RETRY.
